composio.note: With Composio's managed Slack app, the install screen and bot identity are Composio's, scopes are Composio's defaults, and the rate-limit budget is shared. Bring your own app to show your bot name and icon in channels, request exactly the bot/user scopes your agent needs, get a per-app rate-limit budget, and poll more often than Composio's 15-minute managed minimum. You also need your own app to ever reach Marketplace status, which is now what unlocks normal conversations.history/replies limits.

verdict.headline: You can create a Slack app and distribute it unlisted the same day, but an agent that reads channel history will be throttled to 1 request/min and 15 messages per call until it is approved for the Slack Marketplace, which needs 10 active workspaces and a review of up to ~12 weeks.
verdict.summary: Creating the app, OAuth install and unlisted public distribution are self-serve with no review. Since May 2025, commercially distributed apps outside the Marketplace get conversations.history and conversations.replies at 1 request/min with a max of 15 objects (internal apps and Marketplace apps exempt). Slack's api.slack.com changelog says this extends to existing installs from 3 March 2026, while the current docs.slack.dev post still says existing installs are not impacted (see uncertain). Marketplace approval needs 10+ active workspaces and preliminary (up to 10 business days) plus functional (up to 10 weeks) review, and Marketplace apps can't use search:read or admin.* scopes.
verdict.time_to_production: Same day for unlisted distribution (history-reading throttled); roughly 3-6 months to Marketplace approval: time to reach 10 active workspaces (yours to control) + up to 10 business days preliminary + up to 10 weeks functional review
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for app + Composio; 1-3 days to prepare a Marketplace submission (demo video, test accounts, scope justifications) (estimates)
verdict.approval_wait: None for single-workspace or unlisted distribution. Marketplace: preliminary review up to 10 business days, functional review up to 10 weeks for new submissions (6 weeks for resubmissions of published apps); cannot be expedited. Some customer workspaces also require admin approval to install.

phases.name: Create the app from a manifest
phases.goal: A Slack app with bot/user scopes and Composio's redirect URL configured.

steps.title: Generate the app manifest
steps.detail: Manifest keys: oauth_config.redirect_urls (max 1000), oauth_config.scopes.bot and oauth_config.scopes.user (max 255 each), settings.token_rotation_enabled. Typical agent bot scopes: chat:write, channels:history, groups:history, im:history, mpim:history; user scope search:read only if the agent must search (user token only, not allowed in Marketplace apps).
steps.agent_help: Agent can generate the manifest YAML with the scopes below and Composio's redirect URL, URL-encode it, and give you a one-click link https://api.slack.com/apps?new_app=1&manifest_yaml=<encoded>.

steps.title: Create the app in your workspace
steps.detail: Open the manifest link while logged in, pick your development workspace and confirm. (apps.manifest.create can also do this with an app configuration token, which expires after 12 hours.)
steps.agent_help: Agent prepares the link; you log in and click Create.

steps.title: Decide on token rotation before going live
steps.detail: Without rotation, Slack tokens never expire. With rotation, access tokens expire after 12 h and each refresh token is single-use, and rotation can never be turned off. Only enable it if your token store (or Composio) refreshes reliably.
steps.agent_help: Agent can check whether your Composio auth config handles refresh and set token_rotation_enabled in the manifest.

phases.name: Connect to Composio
phases.goal: Composio installs your app instead of its managed one.

steps.title: Create a custom auth config
steps.detail: Copy Client ID and Client Secret from Basic Information. Composio dashboard > Auth Configs > Create Auth Config > Slack > OAuth2; paste them; use the ac_... id via auth_configs={"slack": "ac_..."}.
steps.agent_help: Agent writes the session code; you paste the secret.

steps.title: Register Composio's redirect URL
steps.detail: Add https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback under OAuth & Permissions > Redirect URLs (or in the manifest). Some toolkits still default to legacy https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, so copy the URI the Composio dashboard shows. Slack requires HTTPS, no '#' anchor, and a match or subdirectory of a configured URL.
steps.agent_help: Agent includes it in oauth_config.redirect_urls and verifies it against the dashboard value.

phases.name: Test in your workspace
phases.goal: Your workspace installs via OAuth and the agent can post and read.

steps.title: Install via the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Run Composio's connect flow against your dev workspace. Bot scopes go in scope and user scopes in user_scope. Scopes are additive across installs and can't be downgraded. Auth codes expire after 10 minutes.
steps.agent_help: Agent generates the connect link and then calls chat.postMessage and conversations.history to verify.

steps.title: Measure history-read behaviour
steps.detail: Before distribution, check how your agent reads context. Once distributed outside the Marketplace, conversations.history/replies return at most 15 objects and allow 1 call/min, so design for incremental reads (Events API) rather than re-reading channels.
steps.agent_help: Agent can refactor context fetching to cache messages and use event-driven updates, and add 429 handling.

phases.name: Distribute unlisted
phases.goal: Any workspace can install via OAuth (no Slack review).

steps.title: Activate Public Distribution
steps.detail: Manage Distribution > 'Share Your App with Other Workspaces': complete the checklist (OAuth implemented, HTTPS on redirect/request URLs) and click Activate Public Distribution. Without it, other workspaces get invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app.
steps.agent_help: Agent can confirm every URL is HTTPS and the OAuth flow works end-to-end before you click.

steps.title: Customer admin approval
steps.detail: Some workspaces require admin approval for app installs; requesting fewer scopes helps.
steps.agent_help: Agent can draft a scope-by-scope justification for admins.

phases.name: Slack Marketplace review
phases.goal: Marketplace approval: direct installs and normal history rate limits.
phases.duration: Weeks to months; up to ~12 weeks of review after you qualify

steps.title: Reach 10 active workspaces
steps.detail: Submission requires installs on 10+ workspaces active in the past 28 days, with the app fully tested on a non-development workspace including uninstall. Since July 2026 the app must also stay at 10+ installed workspaces for the whole review (the threshold was temporarily 5 from August 2025).

steps.title: Prepare and submit
steps.detail: Request only scopes for features that exist today; explain each scope; no admin.*, search:read or triggers:* scopes. Provide test credentials with dummy data and ideally a demo video of install, OAuth, setup, use and uninstall.
steps.agent_help: Agent drafts scope justifications, test-account instructions and the demo script; you record and submit.

steps.title: Wait for preliminary and functional review
steps.detail: Preliminary feedback up to 10 business days; functional review up to 10 weeks (6 weeks for resubmissions of published apps). Resubmitting during preliminary review resets your queue position; launch dates can't be expedited.

requirements.item: Slack workspace where you can create apps
requirements.detail: The app is created in a development workspace.
Must be HTTPS, no anchor, and match (or be a subdirectory of) a configured Redirect URL.

requirements.item: Public distribution activated; SSL on all app URLs
requirements.detail: OAuth redirect, interactivity, options-load and Events API URLs must support SSL.

requirements.item: 10+ active workspaces, test credentials, minimal justified scopes
requirements.detail: Marketplace submission prerequisites; installs must stay at 10+ throughout the review; demo video recommended.

scopes.review_impact: No review for unlisted; normal Marketplace scope review.

scopes.purpose: Read public/private channel, DM and group DM history for context.
scopes.review_impact: No review to request, but conversations.history/replies drop to 1 req/min and 15 objects for non-Marketplace distributed apps; must be justified in Marketplace review.

scopes.purpose: Search messages across the workspace (search.messages, Tier 2).
scopes.review_impact: User-token only; listed as not allowed for Slack Marketplace apps.
Not allowed in Marketplace apps; avoid for agents.

oauth.pkce: Supported (generally available since 30 March 2026): enable it in app settings or with oauth_config.pkce_enabled in the manifest. Enabling it marks the app as a public client and is one-way; PKCE parameters are optional for web redirect URLs but required for custom URI schemes, and refresh tokens issued to PKCE-enabled apps expire after 30 days. A server-side confidential client such as Composio's callback does not need it.
oauth.refresh_tokens: By default tokens never expire (revoked via auth.revoke, uninstall, or user deactivation). With token rotation enabled (irreversible), access tokens expire after 12 h (expires_in 43200); refresh with oauth.v2.access grant_type=refresh_token; each refresh is done with the latest refresh token, and the used refresh token is revoked.
oauth.redirect_uri_rules: HTTPS only; must match or be a subdirectory of a configured Redirect URL; no '#' anchors; if several are configured, send the same redirect_uri to authorize and oauth.v2.access or get bad_redirect_uri; default is the first configured URL. Up to 1000 redirect URLs via manifest.

limits.limit: conversations.history and conversations.replies: 1 request/minute, max 15 objects per call
limits.applies_when: Commercially distributed apps not approved for the Marketplace. New apps/installs since 29 May 2025; existing installs from 3 March 2026 per the api.slack.com changelog (the docs.slack.dev post says existing installs are not impacted). Internal customer-built apps keep 50+/min and 1,000 objects.
limits.how_to_lift: Get approved for the Slack Marketplace.

limits.limit: chat.postMessage: about 1 message/second per channel (special tier)
limits.applies_when: Agent posting bursts into one channel

limits.limit: Tier 2 (20+/min) for search.messages; tiers are the same on all Slack plans

blockers.fix: Activate Public Distribution under Manage Distribution.
Register the exact Composio callback (HTTPS) and send the same redirect_uri in both steps.

blockers.blocker: Scope not approved for published app
blockers.fix: Request only scopes approved for the app, or resubmit with the new scope justified.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 429 on conversations.history/replies; the agent only sees ~15 recent messages and loses thread context
blockers.fix: Cache messages from the Events API, read incrementally, and pursue Marketplace approval.

blockers.symptom: token_expired / invalid_auth about 12 hours after install
blockers.fix: Refresh before expiry and always store the newest refresh token; rotation cannot be disabled.

agent_can: Generate the app manifest (scopes, redirect URLs, token rotation) and a one-click creation link
Write Composio auth-config session code and verify the redirect URI
Refactor context-reading to work within 1 req/min / 15-object limits
Draft admin-facing scope justifications, Marketplace scope explanations and a demo script
you_must: Log in to Slack and create the app from the manifest
Paste the client secret into Composio
Win 10 active workspaces, then submit to the Marketplace and handle reviewer feedback

uncertain: Official sources conflict on existing installs: the 29 May 2025 changelog post says existing installations of unlisted apps 'will not be impacted', while the api.slack.com changelog entry says the limits apply to existing unlisted installs on 3 March 2026. Plan for the stricter reading.
Whether Composio's managed Slack app is Marketplace-approved (and so exempt from the history throttle) is not documented; don't assume it is.
Slack documents no review for unlisted public distribution; this is inferred from the distribution page contrasting it with reviewed Marketplace apps.
Slack's May 2025 API Terms frame the Marketplace as the appropriate channel for commercial distribution; how strictly this is enforced against unlisted commercial apps is unclear.
Time to production beyond Slack's stated review windows depends on how fast you reach 10 active workspaces; the 3-6 month figure is an estimate.
The token_expired / invalid_auth symptom text for unrefreshed rotated tokens is from general Slack behaviour and was not verified on the fetched rotation page.
The exact Composio redirect URI for the SLACK toolkit (v3 vs legacy v1) should be copied from the dashboard.
